title: SpecArch record, 1.0
description: A record is a fact about one event in the life of a system: a change request, a defect, a release, an incident in production, a commissioning run, an approval, an idea, a communication with a stakeholder, a session (a meeting or a call with its attendance), a test session, a deploy or a test run. Records live in records/ beside the specification's folder, one file per record, in a folder per kind; they point into the specification, and the specification points back only where a decision cites a communication record. A record names people only by role, except the person label a communication record may carry, which the documents for everyone leave out. Every object rejects unknown keys; keys starting with 'x-' are allowed everywhere as extensions.

specarchRecord.description: The record format version this file is written against, in three parts, major.minor.patch: 1.0.0, or a later 1.0 patch, which is read as 1.0. A file on 0.1, the format before 1.0.0 and the same in shape, is checked against specarch-record-0.1.schema.json and read beside 1.0; specarch upgrade moves it to 1.0.0.

kind.description: What the record is; it decides the folder it lives in and the keys it holds.

role.description: A role: the key of a stakeholder of the specification, never a person's name.

name.description: The kebab-case name of an element of the specification, such as a test, an environment, a monitor or a check.

version.description: A Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 version, such as 1.4.0.

recordId.description: The ID of a change request, defect, incident, idea, communication, session, test session or deploy: an upper-case prefix, a dash and a number or name, such as CR-12, DEF-7, INC-3, IDEA-4, COM-9, SES-2, TS-1 or DEP-5. It is the record's file name, or an ID in a tracker declared under the specification's sources.

reference.description: A reference into the specification: a requirement ID such as LIB-5, or a #/ pointer into the merged specification such as #/entities/Loan, #/tests/borrow-limit or #/environments/production.

run.description: A commissioning run, by the name of its record: its date and environment, such as 2026-10-07-production.

change.description: A change request (ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207:2017, 6.4.13; ISO/IEC/IEEE 14764:2022): a request for the system to be different. Kept in records/changes/, named by its ID.

title.description: One line saying what is asked for.

phase.description: Where it was raised: during development, at the user acceptance test on a build that is not released (acceptance), or in production.

seenAt.description: Where the tester saw it: the pointers copied from the trace of the build, before anyone has analysed what changes. Checked to resolve while the record is open.

observed.description: What the tester saw, in their words; no customer data.

expected.description: What the tester expected, in their words.

type.description: The maintenance type of ISO/IEC/IEEE 14764:2022 other than corrective, which is a defect: additive (a new capability), perfective (a better one), adaptive (a new environment) or preventive (a problem headed off).

urgency.description: The change type of ITIL 4 change enablement, which sets how much assessment it gets before approval: standard (pre-approved and low risk), normal or emergency.

reason.description: Why it is asked for, in plain words.

cause.description: Why the result was not what was wanted, written when the change is analysed. omitted: the specification left it out; nobody wrote it and nobody was asked about it. wrong: the specification said it, and it was not what was meant. changed: the specification said what was meant, and the need changed after it was written. unheard: the stakeholder who uses it was absent or never asked when the requirement was taken; pick it when the unheard warning, a session they missed or a communication record shows they were not heard. omitted, wrong and unheard measure the requirements work; changed is normal change.

questions.description: The open questions the analysis wrote, by ID. Text, as a decision's answers are, since an answered question leaves the specification; checked to be questions of the specification while the change is proposed or analysed.

affects.description: What it changes in the specification, written when it is analysed.

adds.description: What it adds: requirement IDs or #/ pointers that resolve once it is implemented.

changes.description: What it changes: requirement IDs or #/ pointers that resolve before and after.

removes.description: What it removes: requirement IDs or #/ pointers that no longer resolve once it is implemented; a removed requirement may instead stay with status retired.

impact.description: The version step it needs under Semantic Versioning 2.0.0: major when a client written for the previous version breaks, minor when the public interface only grows, patch when it does not change.

effort.description: The effort the change takes, in hours, as the team recorded it: estimatedHours when it is analysed, spentHours once it is done. A change whose effort records neither as a positive number is shown as missing in the progress document, never filled in (ADR-227).

estimatedHours.description: The hours the team estimated the change takes, a positive number.

spentHours.description: The hours the team spent on the change, a positive number.

status.description: Where it stands: proposed, analysed (affects and impact written), approved or rejected, implemented (the specification and the code carry it), released, or withdrawn by the requester.

defect.description: A defect: the system not doing what its specification says, the corrective maintenance of ISO/IEC/IEEE 14764:2022. Kept in records/defects/, named by its ID.

title.description: One line saying what goes wrong.

phase.description: Where it was found: during development, at the user acceptance test on a build that is not released (acceptance), or in production.

seenAt.description: Where the tester saw it: the pointers copied from the trace of the build, before anyone has analysed what changes. Checked to resolve while the record is open.

observed.description: What the tester saw, in their words; no customer data.

expected.description: What the tester expected, in their words.

severity.description: How badly it stops the system from meeting its requirements.

violates.description: The requirement IDs, or #/ pointers to the design elements, it breaks.

incidents.description: The incidents it caused, by ID.

status.description: Where it stands: reported; confirmed, not-a-defect or duplicate after triage against the specification; fixed (the fix is merged and the test passes); released.

release.description: A release of the system: one version, what it includes and what accepted it. Kept in records/releases/, named by its version.

status.description: Planned while it is being built, released once it ships, withdrawn if it is pulled.

includes.description: The change requests and defects it carries, by ID.

implementations.description: The version of each implementation file at release, keyed by stack.

commissioning.description: The commissioning runs that accepted it, by record name.

commit.description: The commit the release was built from.

incident.description: An incident in production (ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207:2017, 6.4.12): the live system misbehaving. Kept in records/incidents/, named by its ID.

impact.description: What it did to the people who use the system.

status.description: Open while it lasts, resolved once the system is back to what the specification says.

defects.description: The defects that follow from it, by ID.

changes.description: The change requests that follow from it, by ID.

noChange.description: For a resolved incident that leads to no defect and no change, why.

rollbackUsed.description: Whether the deployment stage's rollback was used.

commissioning.description: One commissioning run: the checks of the commissioning stage run on the installed system. Kept in records/commissioning/, named by its date and environment.

build.description: The build that was installed, such as an image tag or a commit.

results.description: The result of each check, keyed by check name.

note.description: What was seen, or why it was skipped.

signoff.description: Who signed the run off, and when.

approval.description: An approval for code generation, written by specarch approve. Kept in records/approvals/, named by its version.

documents.description: The documents the stakeholder read, by target name.

digest.description: The SHA-256 of every .yaml file of the specification when it was approved.

commit.description: The commit the specification's folder was at when it was approved, written when every file under it was committed to a git repository; diff between it and the working tree shows an approver only what changed since.

citation.description: One citation: which source, where in it, and what it says here, as an element of the specification cites one.

source.description: The key of a source declared under 'sources' in specarch.yaml.

clause.description: The clause, section, page or question cited, as the source numbers it, such as '5.2.5' or 'Annex A'.

says.description: What the source says that applies here, in plain words.

idea.description: An idea: one proposal for the specification, taken in from a conversation, a table, an example, a document, code, a recording or a review before the specification says it, with the element it is about and the text it proposes. A person sets its status; a model or an importer only proposes. An idea comes before the specification says anything; a change request asks for an approved specification to be different. Kept in records/ideas/, named by its ID.

statement.description: One line saying what is proposed.

inputMode.description: How it came in: chat (a conversation about the specification), table (a row of a decision table or a spreadsheet), example (a worked example), document (a passage of a document), code (read from code or a database), voice (a transcribed recording), review (a review comment) or walkthrough (a guided walkthrough, a step-by-step interview over the specification).

cites.description: The declared sources it comes from, one citation each.

location.description: Where in what it came from, when that is no declared source: a conversation's file and turn, a table's row, a review comment's file and line.

about.description: The element it is about: a requirement ID or a #/ pointer. For an element the specification does not have yet, the pointer names where it would go, #/<section>/<name>, such as #/algorithms/reservationFee. Checked while the idea is open; an accepted or rejected idea keeps the pointer it had when it was decided.

text.description: The text it proposes for the specification at about, as YAML; none for an idea that is a statement only.

status.description: Where it stands, set by a person: proposed (taken in), discussed (talked over, not decided), accepted (its text taken into the specification), rejected (nothing taken in, kept with the reason) or question (turned into an open question that a stakeholder decides).

decision.description: The decision on the idea, by a person: accepted or rejected, and why.

why.description: Why it was decided so; for a rejected idea, the reason it was not taken in.

became.description: What it turned into, each by its ID: the decision record that took it in, the open question it became, a change request or a defect.

decision.description: The ID of a decision of the specification, such as ADR-012.

question.description: The ID of a question of the specification, open or answered by a decision, such as Q-12.

instant.description: An instant, quoted, as RFC 3339 writes it with its offset: "2026-10-31T10:15:00+07:00". The offset is the one the clock showed where the event happened; the specification's timeZone is not applied to it.

words.description: What was said: the text, and whether it is the words as given (verbatim) or a summary in the recorder's words.

form.description: verbatim when the text is the words as they were said or written; summary when it is the recorder's summary of them.

evidence.description: The files that show the event happened as recorded: a chat export, an email, minutes, a recording, a screenshot. Each by its path under records/, its media type and its SHA-256, so that a file edited later no longer matches. A record with none was recorded from memory or from a conversation that left no file, and the documents say so.

path.description: The file's path under records/, with slashes, such as evidence/COM-12-chat.txt.

mediaType.description: The file's media type, such as text/plain, image/png or application/pdf.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the file's bytes, as sha256: and 64 hexadecimal digits.

links.description: What the event touches in the specification and in the other records, each list by ID or pointer; at least one list.

questions.description: The questions it is about, open or already answered by a decision, by ID.

decisions.description: The decisions it is about, by ID.

changes.description: The change requests it is about, by ID.

defects.description: The defects it is about, by ID.

ideas.description: The ideas it is about, by ID.

channel.description: How the people met: a meeting, a chat, an email, a call or a document passed.

communication.description: One communication with a stakeholder: something said or written by one side to the other, in a meeting, a chat, an email, a call or a document. Kept in records/communications/, named by its ID; specarch log writes one from what the analyst reports in chat.

direction.description: in when the stakeholder said it to the project, out when the project said it to the stakeholder.

to.description: Who it was said to, by role.

person.description: A label for the person on the stakeholder's side, when the role alone does not say who, such as the morning-shift lead; never a name a document for everyone may show, since those documents leave it out.

type.description: What it is: an answer to a question of the specification (answer), a question the stakeholder asked (question), a request for the system to be different (request), information given by either side (information), or an objection to what was shown or proposed (objection).

reply.description: What the other side said back, when one record holds both: the reply to a question the stakeholder asked.

recordedBy.description: The role that wrote the record down, such as the analyst who reported the conversation.

session.description: The session or test session it was said in, by ID.

source.description: The declared source of the specification it belongs to, by key: the interview it was part of.

links.description: An answer links the question it answers under questions, or the change request it settles under changes (ADR-221); the validator checks that one of them is there.

session.description: One session with stakeholders: a meeting, a call or a workshop, with who was invited and who came, by role. The things said in it are communication records that name it under session. Kept in records/sessions/, named by its ID.

title.description: One line saying what the session was about.

present.description: The roles that took part; a role invited and not here was absent.

recordedBy.description: The role that wrote the record down.

summary.description: What was covered, in plain words.

source.description: The declared source of the specification the session is, by key: an interview.

test-session.description: One test session: a system integration test, a user acceptance test or another kind, on one build in one environment, with who tested and the result. The remarks made in it are communication records that name it under session, and the change requests and defects they became are linked. Kept in records/test-sessions/, named by its ID.

title.description: One line saying what was tested.

level.description: sit for a system integration test, uat for a user acceptance test, other for any other test session.

version.description: The version of the build under test, a release record, planned or released.

build.description: The build that was tested, such as an image tag or a commit.

present.description: The roles that tested; a role invited and not here was absent.

result.description: passed when every planned test passed, failed when one did not, incomplete when the session ended before the planned tests were run.

recordedBy.description: The role that wrote the record down.

summary.description: What was tested and what was seen, in plain words.

deploy.description: One deploy: a version installed in an environment, when, by whom and with what result. A release record says what a version carries; a deploy record says when it was put where. Kept in records/deploys/, named by its ID.

version.description: The version installed, a release record, planned or released.

build.description: The build that was installed, such as an image tag or a commit.

result.description: succeeded when the version runs in the environment, failed when the deploy did not complete, rolled-back when it completed and was then taken back.

note.description: What was seen, in plain words.

buildOfChange.description: The build a remark from acceptance is about: the specification's version (a pre-release one included), the environment it ran in, and when known the digest and the commit or build id.

digest.description: The specification's digest the build names in its generated files, as the approval record keeps it.

build.description: The commit or build id, as a commissioning or test-session record names it.

buildOfDefect.description: The build a remark from acceptance is about: the specification's version (a pre-release one included), and when known the digest and the commit or build id; the environment is the defect's own.

digest.description: The specification's digest the build names in its generated files, as the approval record keeps it.

build.description: The commit or build id, as a commissioning or test-session record names it.

test-run.description: One run of the tests on one build: where it ran, on what, when, by whom, the results file as its evidence, and one result per test case of that file, each with the test of the specification it maps to. Kept in records/test-runs/, named by its ID; specarch log test-run writes it from a JUnit XML file (ADR-230).

version.description: The version of the build, a release record, planned or released, when the build is one.

build.description: The build that was tested, such as a commit or an image tag with its digest.

digest.description: The digest of the specification the build was generated from, as the approval record and a defect's against keep it.

by.description: The role that ran the tests.

results.description: One result per test case of the results file, in the file's order; several may name one test or element, as subtests and parameterised cases run it more than once.

name.description: The test case's name as the results file writes it.

test.description: The test of the specification the test case runs, by name; left out when it runs an algorithm's or a call mapping's worked examples (element), or when its name maps to no test or to two, which the validator warns of (test_unmapped).

element.description: The algorithm, or the path of the operation whose call mapping, the test case runs the worked examples of, as a #/ pointer, such as #/algorithms/late-fee: a test the test generators write for those examples, which no entry under tests names. Its outcome counts for that element.

outcome.description: passed; failed when an assertion did not hold; error when the test could not run to its end; skipped when it was not run.

message.description: What the results file says of a failure, an error or a skip, in one line.

defect.description: The defect this failure opened or belongs to, by ID.
